hypothesis: A dedicated multiclass model trained on every eligible official historical TrackMan pitch can learn pitcher, batter, team, count, and hand interactions that the main-table-only selector and smoothed frequency profiles miss. Better deployable fine-pitch probabilities can recover materially more of the already measured fine-pitch control oracle.

source_protocol.route: all R rows are predicted; exactly linked current-year auto-pitch labels are used only for selector diagnostics
source_protocol.history_cutoff: raw TrackMan and identity mappings use seasons strictly before the target year
source_protocol.candidate: one raw-TrackMan CatBoost recipe geometrically blended with the locked parent selector
source_protocol.ranking: minimize worst source log-loss, then mean log-loss, then maximize minimum top-1 improvement, then smaller raw-model weight
source_protocol.on_fail: Close without reading 2022+ selector labels or any control-success metric.
source_protocol.on_pass: Freeze the selector blend and preregister one downstream fine-pitch-expert marginalization before reading control-success metrics.
